newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia arrests suspect in NZ parcel bombing.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia arrests suspect in NZ parcel bombing.

text.p: Malaysian police have arrested a man in connection with a parcel bomb explosion which injured two students in New Zealand last month, the national news agency Bernama reported on Friday.

The 30-year-old suspect, who works for a submarine oil pipeline repair company in Saudi Arabia, surrendered to police in Kuala Lumpur after learning from his family he was being sought in connection with the bomb case, Bernama said.
It quoted Malaysian criminal investigations director Said Awang as saying a New Zealand police official would travel to Malaysia soon following the arrest.

In the October 30 incident in Wellington, Malaysian students Hui Mei Kueh, 20, and Ken Kok, 25, were injured in their car when a parcel, which Hui had just collected from a courier firm, exploded upon opening.
The A4-envelope-sized parcel, containing a bomb made of chemical powder, was addressed to Hui, a female student.
Malaysian police believe the parcel was mailed from Malaysia.
